# bare

MCP server in Go, generated by [mcpgen](https://github.com/alesr/mcpgen) vgolden.
Targets MCP spec **2026-07-28** on `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` v1.8.0.

Generated MCP server.

## Run

```sh
go run ./cmd/bare            # serves http://localhost:8080/mcp
go run ./cmd/bare -addr :9090 # custom address
```

## Develop

```sh
make check         # tidy → fmt → vet → build → test
make conformance   # official MCP conformance suite against a local instance (needs node/npx)
```

Or with mcpgen itself:

```sh
mcpgen check . --json        # structured verdict; exit 0 = green
mcpgen add tool spec.json    # add a capability without touching registration files
```

## Structure

- `cmd/bare/main.go` — entrypoint
- `internal/mcpapp/` — server wiring (mcpgen-owned) + registration files with
  `mcpgen:begin/end` markers
- `internal/mcpapp/tools/handlers/` — one user-owned file per tool
- `internal/mcpapp/prompts/`, `internal/mcpapp/resources/` — same pattern
- `mcpgen.json` — single source of truth (tools, prompts, resources, features)
- `server.json` — MCP Registry descriptor (OCI package block)

## Security checklist

Before exposing this server beyond localhost:

- [ ] Put an authenticating proxy / OAuth in front of the HTTP transport
      (see the optional `oauth` feature block: RFC 9728 protected-resource
      metadata, RFC 8707 resource indicators, CIMD instead of deprecated DCR).
- [ ] Never log tool arguments that may contain secrets.
- [ ] Keep the SDK pinned and current; MCP moves quarterly.
- [ ] Run `make conformance` and `mcpgen check --json` in CI (already wired).
- [ ] For the EU AI Act high-risk obligations (logging, audit, oversight),
      keep request logs at the transport layer, not inside tool handlers.

## Registry

`server.json` is a valid MCP Registry descriptor. Publishing is done with the
registry's own tooling; the OCI identifier in `server.json` must point at the
image built from the `Dockerfile`.
